method:
Manage — exhaustion study for HELD positions (Setups > Manage sub-tab).

Question it answers, per asset and side: "I am long X and the trend is with me.
When exhaustion signal S fires, do forward returns actually weaken versus just
staying in?" Everything is drift-adjusted the same way as signal_study.py:

  * baseline  = all days since 2015 with the trend score in the position's
                favour (score x side > +0.2) — i.e. the return you get by simply
                holding through the trend
  * per signal: onset dates (first day the condition is true, min 10 trading
                days apart, trend in favour at onset), forward return over
                1W/2W/1M/3M in the POSITION's direction, mean vs baseline mean,
                placebo p (2000 draws of n dates from the baseline pool; p_weak =
                share of placebos at least as WEAK as the signal), and the mean
                worst drawdown over the next 1M (MAE)
  * verdict:    LIGHTEN  p_weak <= 0.05 & n >= 15  (returns significantly weaker)
                LEAN     p_weak <= 0.15
                ADD      p_weak >= 0.95             (signal preceded STRONGER returns)
                NOISE    otherwise

Signals (long side shown; short side mirrors):
  rsi_roll    RSI14 peaked >= 70 in the last 10 bars and has dropped >= 3 pts
  fast_flip   10/30 speed response crosses below 0 while 40/120 stays > +0.2
  stretch     21d move >= +2 sigma (63d realised vol)
  score_roll  trend score fell >= 0.2 from its 20d max while still > 0.3
  dist50      price >= +2 sigma above its 50d average (vol-scaled)
  macd_x      MACD histogram crosses negative while trend score > 0.3
  rsi_div     price at a 14-bar high while RSI14 is >= 5 pts below its 14-bar max

Held positions: held_positions.json (repo root) — [{ticker, side, note}] in
TICKER space (paid UST 10Y = long the yield ticker). The tab can toggle others
locally. Context (positioning, FV) is read from the existing feeds.

Output: site/manage.json. Run after generate_data.py and the positioning /
FV / CTA feeds (CLAUDE.md step 7e3).
